project: Project 3: India GCC Regulatory Conflict Register
theme: Regulatory Jurisdiction Collision -- Machine-Readable Resolution (GDPR x EU AI Act x DPDPA)
author: Vasu Sharma

statutory_baselines.india_dpdpa: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023) and Draft DPDP Rules 2025

conflicts.dpdpa_section: s.16(1)-(2) (cross-border transfers permitted except to restricted countries); s.17(1)(c) (cross-border processing under contract)
conflicts.eu_ai_act_article: Art. 2(1)(c) (extraterritorial scope for third-country providers/deployers whose output is used in EU)
conflicts.operational_tension: Indian GCC engineering teams frequently access European patient health records, DICOM telemetry, and clinical annotations via cloud consoles and Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) under the operational assumption that viewing data remotely without downloading files locally does not constitute a cross-border transfer. Under EDPB Guidelines 05/2021 and CJEU Schrems II, remote viewing or remote access from a third country is legally identical to a physical data transfer, triggering mandatory Chapter V obligations in the absence of an Indian adequacy decision.
conflicts.resolution_architecture: Execute Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914 Module 2 (Controller-to-Processor) Standard Contractual Clauses supported by a Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA). Enforce Zero Local Persistence VDI controls (Citrix/WorkSpaces display-only; disable local downloads, clipboard sync, printing, and USB mounting) with ephemeral compute nodes that wipe memory on session termination.
conflicts.residual_risk: Medium: Sovereign interception risks under IT Act s.69 neutralized via zero local persistence and encrypted VDI sessions.
conflicts.enforcement_precedent: CNIL 101 Complaints (MED-2022-004); Irish DPC Inquiry into TikTok Technology Ltd (EUR 345M, Sept 2023).

conflicts.conflict_title: Right to Erasure vs. Algorithmic Log Retention
conflicts.gdpr_article: Art. 17 (Right to erasure / right to be forgotten)
conflicts.dpdpa_section: s.8(7) (mandatory erasure upon withdrawal of consent or purpose fulfillment); s.12(3)
conflicts.eu_ai_act_article: Art. 12 & Art. 19 (mandatory automated logging, min. 6 months); Art. 18 (technical documentation retention, 10 years)
conflicts.operational_tension: GDPR Art. 17 and DPDPA s.8(7) mandate immediate erasure of personal data upon patient request or healthcare episode completion. Concurrently, EU AI Act Art. 12 mandates automatic event logging for high-risk clinical AI systems retained for at least 6 months, and Art. 18 mandates 10-year technical file retention. Direct deletion purges regulatory evidence required for post-market surveillance.
conflicts.resolution_architecture: Apply GDPR Art. 17(3)(b) statutory legal obligation exemption. Cryptographically shred the patient re-identification lookup table inside the EU HSM, while retaining decoupled, anonymous operational telemetry in an immutable Frankfurt WORM audit store for statutory AI Act duration.
conflicts.scc_module_applicable: Module 2: Cl. 8.5 (erasure or return of personal data upon completion)
conflicts.residual_risk: Low: Re-identification impossible post-key-shredding; audit logs preserved for medical device vigilance.
conflicts.enforcement_precedent: CNIL Sanction SAN-2023-018 against Criteo (EUR 40M, June 2023) for failure to operationalize erasure in event telemetry.

conflicts.dpdpa_section: s.16(1) (Central Government transfer whitelist/blacklist mechanism); s.17(2)(a)
conflicts.operational_tension: India has no adequacy decision under GDPR Art. 45. While DPDPA s.16 permits transfers except to blacklisted jurisdictions, GDPR Art. 46 requires appropriate safeguards. Standard signed SCCs are contractual only and cannot bind Indian sovereign authorities exercising statutory surveillance powers.
conflicts.resolution_architecture: Execute modular Standard Contractual Clauses (Decision 2021/914 Module 2/3) supported by an empirical Clause 14 Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) and mandatory supplementary technical measures (split-key HSM encryption and edge pseudonymization).
conflicts.residual_risk: Medium: Mitigated through split-key architecture ensuring raw data cannot be decrypted inside the third country.
conflicts.enforcement_precedent: CJEU Case C-311/18 (Schrems II); Irish DPC / EDPB Binding Decision 01/2023 against Meta Platforms (EUR 1.2B fine).

conflicts.conflict_title: Mandatory DPIA vs. Local Fiduciary Discretion
conflicts.dpdpa_section: s.10(2)(c)(i) & Rule 13 (periodic DPIA mandatory only for Significant Data Fiduciaries)
conflicts.eu_ai_act_article: Art. 27 (Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment - FRIA); Art. 9 (Risk management system)
conflicts.operational_tension: GDPR Art. 35(3)(b) makes a DPIA mandatory for any large-scale processing of special category health data. In contrast, DPDPA s.10 only mandates DPIAs if the Central Government designates the entity as a Significant Data Fiduciary (SDF). Indian GCC teams often omit DPIAs assuming they are not an SDF, leaving the European deployer exposed to strict liability.
conflicts.resolution_architecture: Adopt unified dual-regime DPIA module standardizing to the strictest EU benchmark (GDPR Art. 35 + EU AI Act Art. 27 FRIA), satisfying DPDPA Section 10 proactively regardless of formal Indian SDF notification status.
conflicts.scc_module_applicable: Module 2: Cl. 8.6 (assistance with controller DPIAs and prior consultation)
conflicts.residual_risk: Low: Fully harmonized documentation satisfies both EU lead DPA and Data Protection Board of India.
conflicts.enforcement_precedent: Italian Garante Sanction 9870832 against Enel Energia (EUR 79.1M, Feb 2024) for algorithmic processing without DPIA.

conflicts.conflict_title: DPO Mandate vs. Resident Grievance Officer
conflicts.gdpr_article: Art. 37 (Designation of the Data Protection Officer), Art. 38, Art. 39
conflicts.dpdpa_section: s.10(2)(a) (Resident DPO answerable to Board for SDFs); s.8(9) & Rule 9 (Resident Grievance Officer for all fiduciaries)
conflicts.eu_ai_act_article: Art. 4 (AI literacy); Art. 17 (Quality management system accountability)
conflicts.operational_tension: GDPR Art. 37 mandates an independent DPO reporting to the highest management level for large-scale health data processing. DPDPA s.10(2)(a) requires an India-resident DPO for SDFs, while s.8(9) requires a local Grievance Officer. Dual reporting structures risk conflicting instructions and jurisdictional friction during investigations.
conflicts.resolution_architecture: Establish a dual-tier governance hierarchy: EU Group DPO retains independent statutory authority over EU data processing policy; Indian GCC designates an India-resident Grievance Redressal Officer operating under defined SLAs for local principal inquiries.
conflicts.scc_module_applicable: Module 2: Cl. 8.7 (appoint competent compliance contact points)
conflicts.residual_risk: Low: Clear functional separation between global regulatory policy and local operational grievance handling.
conflicts.enforcement_precedent: EDPB Guidelines 07/2020 on concepts of controller and processor; Belgian DPA DPO independence ruling.

conflicts.dpdpa_section: s.4(1) (purpose-specific processing); s.8(3) (accuracy where data drives decisions)
conflicts.eu_ai_act_article: Art. 10(2)-(3) (training, validation and testing datasets must be representative, complete, and free of errors)
conflicts.operational_tension: GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) strictly prohibits collecting or retaining more patient data than is strictly necessary for immediate healthcare delivery. Concurrently, EU AI Act Art. 10(3) mandates that clinical AI training datasets must be representative of demographic cohorts (age, gender, ethnicity) to prevent algorithmic bias. Collecting demographic attributes solely for model tuning conflicts with clinical data minimization.
conflicts.resolution_architecture: Implement synthetic cohort oversampling and federated cross-site validation pipelines. Execute algorithmic bias audits in an isolated sandbox under EU AI Act Art. 10(5) with pseudonymized demographic proxy masks, severing direct patient linkage.
conflicts.residual_risk: Medium: Balancing representative sample size against minimization mandates; managed via statistical power tests.
conflicts.enforcement_precedent: Clearview AI (Dutch AP, Sept 2024, EUR 30.5M) for ingesting mass training data without legal basis.

conflicts.dpdpa_section: s.8(1) (fiduciary liability for processor); s.8(2) (valid contract requirement)
conflicts.eu_ai_act_article: Art. 26 (Deployer obligations); Art. 25 (Responsibilities along the AI value chain)
conflicts.operational_tension: Under GDPR Art. 28, the Indian GCC acts strictly as a data processor executing documented controller instructions. However, under EU AI Act Art. 26, the entity deploying and configuring an AI system exercises operational oversight duties. If the GCC modifies model weights or adjusts inference thresholds, it risks qualifying as an AI provider under Art. 25, creating an uncontracted liability vacuum.
conflicts.resolution_architecture: Execute a tripartite Master Services Agreement and Data Processing Addendum explicitly decoupling roles: EU hospital remains Controller and Deployer; Indian GCC operates strictly as technical Processor and AI Support Provider under locked configuration boundaries.
conflicts.residual_risk: Low: Contractual firewalls prohibit autonomous model hyperparameter retraining without prior controller sign-off.
conflicts.enforcement_precedent: Irish DPC Inquiry into Meta Platforms (EUR 390M, Jan 2023) for role and legal-basis misclassification.

conflicts.gdpr_article: Art. 33 (72 hours to lead supervisory authority), Art. 34 (communication to data subjects)
conflicts.dpdpa_section: s.8(6) & Rule 7 (breach reporting without delay, detailed report within 72 hours); CERT-In Directions 2022 (mandatory 6-hour cybersecurity incident window)
conflicts.eu_ai_act_article: Art. 73 (serious incident reporting within 15 calendar days; 10 days if death; 2 days for critical infrastructure)
conflicts.operational_tension: Indian CERT-In cybersecurity directions mandate reporting security incidents within 6 hours. DPDPA Rule 7 mandates notice to the Board 'without delay' followed by a detailed report within 72 hours. GDPR Art. 33 mandates 72-hour DPA notice. EU AI Act Art. 73 sets a 15-day serious incident window. Multiple conflicting clocks create chaos during an active triage event.
conflicts.resolution_architecture: Implement a unified 4-hour internal escalation SLA within the GCC Security Operations Center (SOC). A single severity-1 triage event triggers parallel automated statutory incident workflows: CERT-In (6h), DPDPA (without delay), GDPR (72h), and AI Act (15d).
conflicts.scc_module_applicable: Module 2: Cl. 8.6(b) (immediate notification to controller upon confirmed security incident)
conflicts.residual_risk: Low: Standardized 4-hour internal escalation ensures all downstream external statutory clocks are met.
conflicts.enforcement_precedent: EDPB Guidelines 9/2022 on personal data breach notification; Irish DPC Twitter fine (EUR 450k) for late breach notification.

conflicts.conflict_title: Special Category Health Data vs. Indian SDF Scope
conflicts.gdpr_article: Art. 9 (Processing of special categories of personal data - health and biometric data)
conflicts.dpdpa_section: None (DPDPA lacks a sensitive personal data category); s.8(5) (general reasonable security safeguards)
conflicts.eu_ai_act_article: Art. 10(5) (special category health data in AI bias auditing); Annex III Point 5(d) (emergency healthcare triage)
conflicts.operational_tension: GDPR Art. 9 imposes a general prohibition on processing clinical health and biometric data unless specific exceptions (Art. 9(2)(h) healthcare delivery, 9(2)(i) public health) apply. DPDPA 2023 deliberately eliminated the sensitive personal data classification found in earlier drafts, treating health data under baseline fiduciary duties. GCC engineers default to handling health data as general personal data.
conflicts.resolution_architecture: Sever all direct patient identifiers (Name, DOB, MRN) at the European edge before transmission. The Indian GCC receives and processes only pseudonymized, encrypted clinical feature tensors and DICOM arrays, with re-identification tables locked in Frankfurt.
conflicts.scc_module_applicable: Module 2: Cl. 8.4 (specific safeguards for special category data); Annex I.B
conflicts.residual_risk: Low: GCC possesses zero re-identification capability; satisfies GDPR Art. 9 and exceeds DPDPA s.8(5).
conflicts.enforcement_precedent: Conseil d'Etat / CNIL Doctolib Health Hosting Decision (CE No. 450163, March 2021) requiring edge key isolation for health data.

conflicts.gdpr_article: Art. 32 (Security of processing - confidentiality and integrity)
conflicts.dpdpa_section: s.17(2)(a) (State exemptions for national security/sovereignty); IT Act 2000 s.69 (interception and decryption orders)
conflicts.eu_ai_act_article: Art. 15 (Cybersecurity and robustness standards for high-risk AI)
conflicts.operational_tension: Section 69 of India's Information Technology Act, 2000 empowers government agencies to issue intercept and decryption orders to any entity holding digital data. Complying with an Indian sovereign interception order directly breaches GDPR Art. 32 confidentiality and SCC Clause 14 commitments.
conflicts.resolution_architecture: Cryptographic key isolation: Master root decryption keys are hosted exclusively in a Frankfurt FIPS 140-3 Level 3 Dedicated Hardware Security Module (HSM). The Indian GCC holds only ephemeral micro-tokens; even if Indian authorities compel GCC disclosure, the GCC physically cannot decrypt raw health records.
conflicts.scc_module_applicable: Module 2: Cl. 14 (local laws and practices), Cl. 15 (notification of government requests)
conflicts.residual_risk: Low: Technical impossibility of compliance eliminates legal risk of foreign intelligence interception.
conflicts.enforcement_precedent: CJEU Case C-311/18 (Schrems II); French Conseil d'Etat Doctolib AWS decision (client-side key isolation).

conflicts.gdpr_article: Art. 28(2) (Specific or general written authorization for sub-processors), Art. 28(4)
conflicts.dpdpa_section: s.8(2) (Data Fiduciary may engage a data processor under a valid contract)
conflicts.eu_ai_act_article: Art. 25(4) (Third-party AI component suppliers must provide documentation and technical support under contract)
conflicts.operational_tension: Indian GCCs frequently subcontract infrastructure, cloud compute, or annotation tooling to local third-party vendors without prior controller sign-off. Under GDPR Art. 28(2), engaging any sub-processor without prior written authorization invalidates transfer legality. DPDPA s.8(2) lacks explicit sub-processor notification mechanisms.
conflicts.resolution_architecture: Contractual flow-down under SCC Module 2/3 Clause 9: Enforce mandatory 30-day prior written controller notice for any new sub-processor, with right to object. Mandatory pass-through of identical GDPR Art. 28(3) and AI Act Art. 25 technical safeguards to all Indian sub-processors.
conflicts.scc_module_applicable: Module 2 & Module 3: Clause 9 (Use of sub-processors); Annex III (Authorized sub-processors)
conflicts.residual_risk: Low: Cloud and annotation vendors pre-vetted and documented in SCC Annex III.
conflicts.enforcement_precedent: French CNIL sanction against Free Mobile (EUR 300k) for unauthorized sub-processor transfers.

conflicts.conflict_title: Model Weight Extraction and Trade Secret Protection
conflicts.gdpr_article: Art. 15 (Right of access by the data subject), Art. 12
conflicts.dpdpa_section: s.11(1) (Right to obtain summary of personal data and processing activities); s.11(2)
conflicts.eu_ai_act_article: Art. 13 (Transparency and provision of information to deployers); Art. 86 (Right to explanation of individual decision-making)
conflicts.operational_tension: Patients invoking GDPR Art. 15 or DPDPA s.11 may demand full visibility into how their data shaped an AI model. Under EU AI Act Art. 86, individuals subject to high-risk decisions have a right to clear explanation. Engineering teams fear disclosing proprietary deep learning weights and trade secrets.
conflicts.resolution_architecture: Fulfill transparency obligations through standardized YAML Model Governance Cards (system boundaries, demographic representation, performance benchmarks, and SHAP/LIME feature importance explanations) without exporting raw neural network weights or proprietary architecture binaries.
conflicts.scc_module_applicable: Module 2: Cl. 8.3 (assistance in responding to data subject requests)
conflicts.residual_risk: Low: Technical explainability cards satisfy Art. 15 and Art. 86 without trade secret exposure.
conflicts.enforcement_precedent: CJEU Case C-634/21 (SCHUFA Holding, Dec 2023) on algorithmic transparency vs trade secret balance.

conflicts.conflict_title: Algorithmic Bias Testing on Sensitive Attributes
conflicts.gdpr_article: Art. 9(1) (Prohibition on processing special categories of data), Art. 9(2)
conflicts.dpdpa_section: s.4(1) (Processing strictly for specified consensual purpose); s.7 (listed legitimate uses)
conflicts.eu_ai_act_article: Art. 10(5) (Express statutory derogation permitting processing of special category data strictly for bias detection and correction)
conflicts.operational_tension: To audit clinical AI models for sex, racial, or geriatric bias, engineers must test models against sensitive personal attributes. However, GDPR Art. 9 strictly limits processing special category data, and DPDPA s.6 restricts use to the original consensual purpose. Testing without statutory grounding is unlawful.
conflicts.resolution_architecture: Utilize the specific statutory derogation under EU AI Act Art. 10(5): Process special category health attributes strictly in an isolated, secure bias testing sandbox with state-of-the-art pseudonymization. Once bias metrics are calculated, test cohorts are immediately shredded; personal attributes are never incorporated into production model weights.
conflicts.residual_risk: Medium: Rigorous governance required to guarantee bias testing data never bleeds into production weights.
conflicts.enforcement_precedent: Clearview AI (Dutch AP, Sept 2024) and Italian Garante OpenAI inquiries regarding unlawful training data processing.

conflicts.gdpr_article: Art. 48 (Transfers or disclosures not authorised by Union law)
conflicts.dpdpa_section: s.36 (Central Government power to call for information); IT Act s.69
conflicts.operational_tension: Indian regulatory bodies or law enforcement may issue statutory orders under s.36 DPDPA or s.69 IT Act demanding production of databases held at the GCC. GDPR Art. 48 states that foreign court judgments or administrative orders cannot legitimize a data transfer unless grounded in an international agreement (e.g. MLAT).
conflicts.resolution_architecture: Operationalize SCC Clause 15: GCC contractually commits to promptly notify the EU controller of any government demand, verify the legality of the request, and exhaust all available legal remedies to challenge unlawful disclosure before releasing data. Technical HSM key separation renders involuntary production computationally impossible.
conflicts.scc_module_applicable: Module 2: Clause 15.1 (Notification of government requests), Clause 15.2 (Review of legality)
conflicts.residual_risk: Low: Split-key HSM architecture ensures the GCC cannot decrypt or produce raw patient data even under compulsion.
conflicts.enforcement_precedent: CJEU Case C-311/18 (Schrems II); EDPB Recommendations 01/2020 on supplementary transfer measures.

conflicts.gdpr_article: Art. 32(1)(a) (Pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data)
conflicts.eu_ai_act_article: Art. 15(1) (Appropriate level of cybersecurity and technical resilience)
conflicts.operational_tension: Standard cloud encryption leaves encryption keys hosted in the same cloud tenant or geography as the compute instance. In a cross-border India-EU pipeline, this allows cloud providers or local administrators to decrypt data under third-country legal compulsion, violating Schrems II requirements.
conflicts.resolution_architecture: Implement envelope encryption with dual-custody key management: Root master keys are provisioned in a dedicated European HSM (Frankfurt). Data is encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) and in transit (TLS 1.3). The Indian GCC receives only ephemeral data encryption keys (DEKs) wrapped by the EU root key, expiring upon session termination.
conflicts.scc_module_applicable: Module 2: Cl. 8.6 (technical and organisational measures); Annex II (Technical safeguards)
conflicts.residual_risk: Low: Validated under EDPB Recommendations 01/2020 Use Case 1 (Encryption in transit and at rest with EU key custody).
conflicts.enforcement_precedent: Conseil d'Etat Doctolib decision (client-side key management prevents third-country subpoena access).

conflicts.gdpr_article: Art. 22(1) (Right not to be subject to solely automated decision-making producing legal/significant effects)
conflicts.dpdpa_section: None (DPDPA contains no explicit automated decision-making prohibition); s.8(3) (accuracy duty)
conflicts.eu_ai_act_article: Art. 14 (Human oversight of high-risk AI systems); Art. 26(2) (deployer human oversight assignment)
conflicts.operational_tension: GDPR Art. 22 grants patients the right to avoid automated clinical decisions without human intervention. EU AI Act Art. 14 mandates that high-risk medical AI must be designed to enable natural persons to oversee operations, prevent automation bias, and override outputs. DPDPA 2023 has no equivalent provision, leading GCC engineers to deploy fully automated batch triage pipelines.
conflicts.resolution_architecture: Implement a Delayed-Reveal UI architecture: The AI diagnostic prediction, confidence score, and explainability maps are withheld until the attending European clinician completes an independent clinical evaluation. Clinician must explicitly confirm or override AI output before record finalization, creating a verifiable human-in-the-loop audit trail.
conflicts.scc_module_applicable: Module 2: Cl. 8.1(a) (processing strictly in accordance with controller instructions)
conflicts.residual_risk: Low: Architectural enforcement of clinician override completely satisfies GDPR Art. 22 and AI Act Art. 14.
conflicts.enforcement_precedent: Italian Garante Sanction against Enel Energia (algorithmic automated decision-making without human safeguards).

conflicts.dpdpa_section: s.6(1) (Consent limited to specified purpose); s.17(2)(b) (research exemption with strict safeguards)
conflicts.eu_ai_act_article: Art. 10(2)(b) (data origin and original purpose documentation)
conflicts.operational_tension: Indian GCC R&D departments frequently treat client clinical datasets as training fodder to improve internal proprietary foundation models, commercial algorithms, or academic benchmarks. Under GDPR Art. 5(1)(b) and SCC Clause 8.1(a), processors are strictly forbidden from reusing personal data for secondary commercial purposes.
conflicts.resolution_architecture: Hard contractual and technical firewall: SCC Clause 8.1(a) Master Services Agreement explicitly bans any reuse of patient telemetry for GCC model training, benchmarking, or intellectual property generation. Data access is sandboxed in ephemeral VDI sessions with zero data export rights.
conflicts.residual_risk: Low: Contractual prohibition reinforced by data leakage prevention (DLP) and network egress blocks.
conflicts.enforcement_precedent: Clearview AI (Dutch AP, Sept 2024, EUR 30.5M) for unlawful commercial scraping and model training reuse.
